title: Negotiate /v1/chat.completions stop/logprobs + stream heartbeat and structured tool-call framing
author: Ravi Singh
release_notes: Adds negotiation for stop/logprobs envelope, introduces stream heartbeat + small framing changes to stable tool-call JSON mode for /v1/chat.completions parity. Backwards compatible with existing client SDKs.
description: Context and motivation: Customers using the OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat.completions adapter reported intermittent loss of final token logprobs and mismatches when mixing legacy stop arrays with structured tool-calls. This PR unifies parameter negotiation (stop, max_tokens, logprobs) between the v1 adapter and Redwood's native runtime, and adds a lightweight stream heartbeat/frame marker to prevent incomplete final-event drops in proxying scenarios. The goal is parity with common OpenAI semantics while preserving Redwood-specific structured output and function/tool calling stability. Checklist: - [x] Parameter mapping layer for stop/logprobs/temperature/role aliases - [x] Streaming heartbeat frame + reassembly logic - [x] Deterministic tool-call JSON framing and 'result' envelope for structured outputs - [x] Integration tests for mixed stop+toolcall scenarios - [x] Docs snippet and SDK compatibility notes Commits (summary): - Add negotiation layer that normalizes incoming v1 params and emits runtime options (commit: 1ea7c3) - Implement stream heartbeat frame and reassembly in v1 proxy (commit: 4b2f98) - Deterministic tool-call envelope: wrap tool responses in {"tool_name", "result"} and include call_metadata (commit: d9a11f) - Tests + fixtures for stop/logprobs race conditions (commit: b3f5a2) - Docs + changelog (commit: 6c5d0b) Changed areas (high level): - server/adapters/openai_v1/handler.go: normalize v1 params, negotiation logic - runtime/streaming/heartbeat.go: heartbeat/frame markers and reassembly helpers - api/compat/chat_params.go: aliasing for roles, stop normalization - runtime/output/tool_envelope.go: structured tool-call framing and serializer - sdk/python/openai_compat.py: param sanitizer + compatibility flag - tests/integration/chat_parity_test.go: new test cases Illustrative snippet (negotiation mapping): """ // pseudo Go mapping: if v1Req.Stop != nil { normalized.Stop = coerceToStringArray(v1Req.Stop) } if v1Req.Logprobs != nil { normalized.IncludeLogprobs = v1Req.Logprobs > 0 } // alias roles: 'system'|'assistant'|'user' -> internal enums """ Review conversation (condensed): - Amelia Carter (reviewer): "Please ensure stop normalization preserves empty-string stops and multiple stop tokens; also add a test for stop appearing as single string vs array." - Author (Ravi): "Added coercion helper and a fixture that covers empty string + single-item array cases." - Jordan Kim: "Stream framing looks good but I'm concerned about heartbeat frequency when proxying across busy gateways." - Author: "Heartbeat interval defaults to 250ms and is configurable via server config; added config doc and a test that simulates a congested proxy." - Priya Patel: "Need to ensure tool-call envelope doesn't break existing SDK consumers who expect raw tool payloads." - Author: "SDKs updated to detect new envelope via compatibility flag; default behavior maintains old surface for customers not opting into 'structured_tooling' flag." CI and testing notes: - Initial CI run: unit tests passed, integration suite failed (race in final-logprobs flush) - Reproduced locally, fixed by explicit flush on stream terminal event and delaying heartbeat teardown by 50ms - Final CI: all checks passed (lint, unit, integration, e2e-flow) Merge decision and method: - Merge state: merged via squash on 2026-02-23 by maintainers - Rationale: fixes multiple customer-reported parity gaps and stabilizes streaming proxy behavior for tool-calls Risk and compatibility notes: - No breaking changes by default. New semantics behind an opt-in 'structured_tooling' flag; v1 adapter will auto-negotiate for common cases but falls back to legacy framing if requested via headers. - Potential perf impact: extra heartbeat frames add ~0.2% extra bandwidth for busy streams; batching and compression mitigate cost. Follow-ups / TODOs: - Roll out SDK compatibility flags in TypeScript + Go (work items linked) - Monitor production errors for first two weeks after deploy and add telemetry for dropped final-events - Consider exposing negotiation diagnostics via Console for debugging merge-time failures Related work items: ENG-4121 (param negotiation), ENG-4180 (streaming robustness), SUP-987 (customer case).
notes: This PR was intentionally conservative: negotiation code tries to preserve existing behaviors unless the 'structured_tooling' opt-in is enabled. Heat-tested on benchmark-lab with mixed toolcall/stop workloads; observed 8-12% reduction in dropped final-event incidents in synthetic proxies.
